source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Make sure the Environmental Protection Agency, or EPA, requires the water system to monitor for the contaminant. Drinking water providers are required to monitor for some contaminants on a daily, monthly or quarterly basis. To do so, water plants buy testing kits and send out water samples to an accredited laboratory, for the most part.
3. If there is no instruction to test for a contaminant in the state's Administrative Code, Title 53, the EPA doesn't require the facility to do so.
4. Once the water system does the tests, the inspecting agency — usually an employee of the state's Environmental Department — will most likely ask to see the results.
5. Water plant staff insert the numbers the laboratory/testing kit returned into the online database of the state.
6. The state then compares test results with concentrations listed in its Administrative Code, Title 53.
7. If tests came back with contaminant levels above
